To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cobinding of fatty acids and synthetic ligands to the orthostere pocket of PPARγ can form a ligand link to the Ω loop, which affects ligand binding and transcriptional activity of PPARγ, thus revealing an alternate ligand binding site near the Ω loop.
cobinding of synthetic and natural ligands to PPARγ can form a ligand link to the omega loop and synergistically alter PPARγ structure and function.
cobinding of the natural/endogenous and synthetic ligands to PPARγ can form a ligand link that synergistically affects the structure and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism of ligand binding to the nuclear receptor PPARγ.
the development of novel ligands for PPARγ, which is a nuclear receptor that plays an important role in lipid metabolism, inflammation, and insulin sensitivity.

the molecular mechanisms by which synthetic ligands can affect the function of nuclear receptors, including the ability of synthetic ligands to affect the binding of natural and endogenous ligands to nuclear receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of synthetic ligands to the orthostetic pocket of the nuclear receptor PPARγ can displace the natural/endogenous ligand from the orthostetic binding pocket to the alternate ligand binding site near the functionaly important omega loop.
the ligand-binding site of a nuclear receptor is a dynamic and flexible pocket that can be occupied by multiple ligands at the same time.
the ligands bind to the receptor in an allosteric manner, which can be competitive or cooperative, depending on the ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ligand link is a new paradigm for the regulation of nuclear receptors by endogenous ligands and synthetic ligands.
synthetic and natural ligands can bind to the orthostetic binding site simultaneously, and the ligands are able to form a link to the omega loop.
the synthetic ligand binds to the orthostetic pocket and pushes the endogenous fatty acid ligand out towards the Ω loop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of multiple ligands to a receptor can lead to a synergistic effect that is not predicted from the binding of a single ligand.
ligand binding is more than just an orthosteric exchange and that synthetic ligands and natural ligands can bind cooperatively and in concert to the same nuclear receptor.
the ligand link between the orthosteric site and the Ω loop may be an important regulatory mechanism for nuclear receptor function.
